result.summary: This PR changes the -acceptnonstdtxn=1 test-network option so that, instead of only relaxing standardness checks that live outside script verification, it also skips non-mandatory script verify flags (STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS beyond MANDATORY), letting transactions using OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS opcodes into the mempool. It refactors CheckInputScripts to take an explicit CheckInputScriptsFor::Block/Mempool discriminator instead of inferring block-vs-mempool context from flag bits, and adds a new GetAllConsensusScriptFlags() plus compile-time/runtime checks ensuring STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS and the accept-nonstd override always remain supersets of whatever GetBlockScriptFlags can return, so a node with this flag set can never keep a consensus-invalid tx cached in its mempool. The change remains restricted to non-mainnet chains.
result.problem: Researchers and developers testing proposed soft-fork features (e.g. OP_CAT, SIGHASH_APO via the inquisition client) currently cannot get mainline Bitcoin Core nodes to accept transactions using those non-standard script features into their mempools, limiting cross-implementation testing on public testnets.

result.card: ajtowns' PR extends the test-net-only -acceptnonstdtxn=1 flag so it also bypasses non-mandatory script verify flags, letting non-standard scripts (OP_NOPx, OP_SUCCESS, etc.) into the mempool, which the author says helps observe transactions using proposed soft-fork features like OP_CAT or SIGHASH_APO on public testnets. It required a substantial CheckInputScripts refactor (explicit Block/Mempool discriminator) and new compile-time/runtime invariants (GetAllConsensusScriptFlags) to guarantee no consensus-invalid tx can end up cached in the mempool even with the flag set. Discussion, spanning two years, included several concept ACKs (benthecarman, glozow, fjahr, ismaelsadeeq, 1440000bytes) and an approach ACK from sedited, with substantial back-and-forth over the CheckInputScripts interface design that the author resolved in a 2026-07-22 push using an enum-based approach. luke-jr's suggestion that the flag should mirror Knots' more conservative =2 semantics remains unaddressed but non-blocking. The change is restricted to non-mainnet chains, limiting its priority relative to mainnet-affecting mempool or validation work, but it does touch validation flag-computation logic that a validation reviewer would need to check carefully.
